chapter_plans.title: The Survivor's Record
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Sofia Bellini is presented as the last surviving witness of the summit and is called to testify before the tribunal.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Sofia Bellini sits before the tribunal, her demeanor calm as she faces officials who see her as a sympathetic survivor. The narrative establishes the deaths at the summit, the system’s chilling power, and Sofia Bellini’s gentle, measured responses. The tribunal leans on the official record, while Pierre Leclerc, posing as a fellow survivor, watches her warily. The chapter closes as Sofia Bellini offers subtle reassurance to the tribunal, reinforcing her role as a helpful, harmless witness.
must_happen: Sofia Bellini is formally introduced as the last surviving witness of the summit.
The tribunal discusses the deaths during the summit, relying on the system's official record.
Pierre Leclerc observes Sofia Bellini's testimony and quietly notes inconsistencies.
[ROMANCE] Elias van Doren, though not present, is referenced as a person who believes in Sofia Bellini’s innocence and is determined to clear her name.
Sofia Bellini offers gentle reassurance to the tribunal and reframes questions to de-escalate tension.
[CLUE C001]
must_not: Reveal or even hint that Sofia Bellini is Nadia Petrescu's daughter or the architect of the system.
Describe any character knowing or suspecting Sofia Bellini’s true motive or secret role.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "Your testimony is all that remains. Why do you think you survived, Sofia Bellini?"
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Pierre Leclerc quietly slips a note under the table, signaling that he wants to speak with Sofia Bellini in secret about what really happened.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: A faint, persistent hum from the recording device in the tribunal chamber makes every word feel permanent.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Dread and isolation, with Sofia Bellini’s warmth masking the tension beneath every official statement.
chapter_plans.spice_note: Psychological intimacy only; no explicit content. The focus is on subtle emotional tension and Elias van Doren’s protective belief in Sofia Bellini.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Establish the tribunal setting and Sofia Bellini’s surface role as a survivor; seed underlying dread and suspicion. Target length: 1600-1900 words.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Sofia Bellini receives Pierre Leclerc’s secret note, setting up their covert meeting and the first hint of cracks in the official narrative.

truth_background: [kernel.true_case] Sofia is Nadia Petrescu's daughter and the architect of the system. She did not survive the summit — she built it. Having watched officials rewrite her mother's testimony until it killed her, Sofia drew the wrong lesson: the weak are those who let themselves be spoken for, and she will never be weak again. She engineered the machine from her mother's case file and ran the summit as a live experiment. Her acts of 'helping' others were always about control. 'Protecting' Elias was never love, but the preservation of her one control variable. Nadia's dying words, 'That is not what I said,' were spoken to Sofia, who was already becoming the system. Sofia took that line and made it the signature of her killing method.
[kernel.core_question] Who truly controls the system that rewrites people to death, and what was Sofia's real role in the tragedy?

chapter_plans.title: Echoes in the Record
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Elias van Doren returns to the tribunal, Sofia Bellini’s interventions shape the testimonies, and the system’s oddities begin to surface.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Elias van Doren arrives at the tribunal, determined to defend Sofia Bellini. As Sofia Bellini reframes another witness’s statement, small changes ripple through the official transcript. The tribunal attributes recent witness deaths to stress or system errors, but Pierre Leclerc grows more suspicious. An archival reference to Nadia Petrescu’s disciplinary hearing is unearthed, but its significance remains veiled. The chapter ends with Sofia Bellini noticing someone has tampered with the official record.

chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: Tribunal notes are marked with tiny, identical corrections in blue ink—no one recalls making them.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Mistrust and subtle intimacy, as Sofia Bellini and Elias van Doren navigate an environment where every word is dangerous.
chapter_plans.spice_note: Emotional tension and micro-beat between Sofia Bellini and Elias van Doren; no explicit content.

chapter_plans.beat_summary: Sofia Bellini continues to gently reframe other witnesses' statements, her guidance always received as benevolent by the tribunal. The chapter closes as Elias van Doren voices his fear that the system itself is dangerous—right as a new correction appears in the record, not matching anyone’s recollection.

chapter_plans.beat_summary: Sofia Bellini’s rapport with Elias van Doren deepens as she offers reassurance in the tribunal chamber, yet she studies his reactions with increasing intensity.
